annotations.text:
Three directions for reading the corpus, all showing the same read (the heatmap video: four inbound links, one overturned finding) so they compare fairly.

Judge on typography, hierarchy and density. Browser zoom does not reach inside an artboard; interaction (claim-to-evidence click, collapsing levels, filters) comes with the built Artifact.

A · MARGINALIA — editorial
One serif reading measure; editor asides, evidence marks, inbound links and the correction all live in the right margin beside the passage they belong to. Keeps browser.html's warm paper palette.

Tradeoff: needs ~1200px; on narrow screens margin notes must fold back inline. A 5,600-word L3 leaves long stretches of empty margin.

B · LEDGER — dense, data-first
Library list always visible on the left, link graph and evidence counts always on the right. Levels are collapsible bands with word counts; asides are labelled inline rows; every id, count and timestamp is monospace.

Tradeoff: the most information per screen and the least pleasure per word. Reading a long L3 in a 760px measure at 14px is work.

C · TWO VOICES — the claim-to-evidence gesture made structural
Argument on the left, the presenter's words on the right; picking a claim brings up the passage it rests on, with the editor's voice set under it in a second typeface. Inbound amendments sit in the header, not a footer.

Tradeoff: reading L3 straight through, in order, becomes a secondary path. Two panes fight below ~1100px.
